system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Oskar Haddad-Lindqvist
oskar.hl@example.com | +46 70 555 0808

Verdane Care
Application: Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) - Patient Experience
Dear Verdane Care hiring team,
Your Patient Experience role closely matches the work I do best: building customer-facing
React and TypeScript features, improving accessibility and mobile performance, and
delivering the Node.js services behind them. I have worked professionally in web development
since 2014 and currently build onboarding features at Älvgrind Fintech. Verdane’s focus on
making booking and intake simpler gives that experience a clear application: helping people
complete important tasks without unnecessary friction.
At Älvgrind, I built a BankID identity verification flow with QR code and same-device
support, error handling and retries. After an initial A/B test with 10% of traffic, the flow was
rolled out fully, increasing onboarding conversion from 61% to 74%. I also reduced mobile
Largest Contentful Paint from 4.1 seconds to 1.9 seconds and implemented WCAG 2.1 AA
accessibility audit fixes. These are directly relevant foundations for your focus on accessible
patient journeys and performance on low-end phones.
My frontend strength is backed by practical NestJS, PostgreSQL and AWS experience. I
helped migrate Express services incrementally to NestJS and built a document-upload flow
using S3 presigned URLs, Lambda virus scanning and SQS. My testing toolkit includes Jest
and Playwright, and I work with Docker and GitHub Actions. Integrating identity verification
and handling uploaded ID documents also provides relevant experience for a product where
personal information needs careful handling.
I collaborate closely with designers in Figma, have mentored at a coding bootcamp, and
served as acting team lead for four months, handling 1:1s and sprint planning. I would
welcome the opportunity to discuss how this combination of frontend depth, full-stack delivery
and team support could contribute to Verdane’s Patient Experience squad. My GitHub link is
included above.
Kind regards,
Oskar Haddad-Lindqvist

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
